sentences.text: The genus Voay contains only one known species, Voay robustus.
Voay skulls are noted for having a distinctive pair of horns on the back of the head, which extend specifically from the squamosal bone.
This animal had a shorter and deeper snout and relatively robust limbs compared to the modern Nile crocodile.
Voay robustus measured approximately 3.5 to 4 meters long and weighed about 170 kilograms.
Estimates suggest the creature could reach a total length of 5 meters while maintaining a weight of 170 kg.
Fossils of Voay have been found at locations including Ambolisatra and Antsirabe in Madagascar.
Voay robustus was originally classified in the genus Crocodylus when it was first described in 1872.
A new genus was created for Voay in 2007 because it did not fit closely enough with the dwarf crocodile to be placed in that genus.
A 2021 paleogenomic study identified Voay as a sister group to Crocodylus, with both lineages diverging in the mid-to-late Oligocene.
Voay lived during the Late Pleistocene and Holocene epochs.
The species lived from 0.129 million years ago until the present Holocene.
It is suggested that Voay went extinct around 2000 years ago alongside other endemic megafauna like the elephant bird after humans arrived in Madagascar.
A hypothesis that Nile crocodiles migrated to Madagascar only after Voay went extinct was disproved by the discovery of 7,500-year-old Nile crocodile fossils contemporaneous with Voay.
